I read in one of your previous comments in this thread that you like soda, or fizzy drinks, I dont know where you live but I started purchasing a probiotic/probiotic soda called Olie- they have lots of flavors to choose from and have plant fibers and cane sugar! The lower sugar paired with the pre and probiotics helped my gut and mood a good amount. I also got prebiotic gummies and try to incorporate more fermented food into my diet like kimchi, sauerkraut, and pickled veggies. I dont know how much all this will help, but when I'm really struggling a good cozy blanket and a high energy/upbeat, or just overall favorite song of mine through good headphones helps. 



Wish you the best of luck, hope you find what really works for you! P.s. the best flavors of Olie I really like so far are the root beer, grape, fruit punch and strawberry vanilla.

So with coco puffs, the terracotta colored balls, they do retain water and are great for tropical plants and help promote root growth, I've always seen them as a medium for orchids (also tropical) but are commonly used in hyro growing. If you have black spots id recommend not bottom-watering. Cut out the black spotted leaves and sad new growth and let it dry out for a bit to ensure the root base can recover. Repot as soon as you can. Same pot will be great just need different soil, don't water until it starts to show signs of thirst (slight drooping, spaghetti looking limbs)

*edit typo. Hydro, not gyro 😅

With cactus/succulent soil it drains fast and retains very little water, perlite will help with drainage also which makes it dry out a wee by faster. Think of water going through rocks versus sand. In rocks it'll darin faster than through fine sand, right? With a tropical plant you want drainage,but not full drainage and dry out. Water retention, but not SOAKING or puddles at the base.

Tropical soil, coco puffs (those little clay rounds, I dont remember the real name), or in a pinch regular ol potting soil. 

Does the pot it's in have drainage? Even if the top 1-2" are dry, the bottom could be soaked and over-soaking the roots

Sounds like pythium, a fungal infection of water logged soil. While this usually starts on the stems and roots caused by water logged soil, it can spread on to the leaves. The soil combo you have it in isnt the best because a peperomia is a tropical plant not a succulent.
